title: String concatenation with + versus StringBuilder
context: Should you build strings with + or with StringBuilder?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: For a single expression, `+` is fine: the compiler turns it into a StringBuilder for you. Inside a loop, each `+` creates a new String, so building n pieces costs O(n²) copying. Use one StringBuilder outside the loop and append inside it. Since Java 9, the compiler uses invokedynamic for concatenation, but loops still need an explicit builder.

points.title: Concatenation in loops
points.why: Each + in a loop copies the whole string again, so the cost grows quadratically.

points.title: Single expressions are fine
points.why: One + expression compiles to efficient code, so no need to avoid it.
